places.name: Target
places.location: 500 N Congress Ave, Lake Park, FL 33403
places.caption: “Got there right after they opened and the place went quite empty and quiet. No issues to report, it’s a big store”

places.name: Mann med liten håndbevegelse
places.caption: “People, walking, without their clothing. Like a nightmare you had that one time”

places.name: Edvard Grieg
places.caption: “Grieg was an impressive composer, it’s even more impressive how much he accomplished without any elbows.”

places.name: Glory, glory with crutches
places.caption: “Good art makes one feel something, and Glory certainly evokes a feeling”

places.name: National Monument for Victims of War 1940-45
places.caption: “What exactly is going on here, and why does it represent what Norway did in the Second World War? It leaves one with a lot of questions”

places.name: Politihesten Tor
places.caption: “Didn’t know that this horse was here and just stumbled upon it. A wonderful surprise”

places.name: Instalacja Jayco
places.caption: “Geometric art which has a certain charm to it”

places.name: Statue of Franklin D. Roosevelt
places.caption: “The American president is plopped atop the hill, with an eternally nice view, fit for a quadruple elected man.”

places.name: Oslo lufthavn
places.caption: “A perfectly fine airport with a decent variety of lighter food options in the International terminal, and a broader selection in the Main terminal area. …”

places.name: WhatSub Sub Shop Palm Beach Gardens
places.location: 10800 N Military Trl #120, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
places.caption: “WhatSub has a selection of Cold and Hot Sandwiches which all seemed to really be quite sizable. I ordered the Chicken Parm, and it had a ton of Chicken on it, served on some great bread”

places.name: Oceana Coffee Drive Thru
places.caption: “Oceana has some decent drip coffee for a fair price. While they have a fairly well sized interior, they also have a drive through as well”

places.name: Sancho Pistola's
places.caption: “Burritos aren’t huge, and are a bit on the pricier side for the area, but they are very tasty.”

places.name: Impresso Express
places.caption: “The drip coffee is ok!”

places.name: JD Vance Mural
places.caption: “It’s hideous, it’s perfect. I love it, the eyes followed me my whole walk home, and may still be following me now”

places.name: Front Street Walls
places.caption: “Beautiful, story-tall murals lining Front Street, under the El”

places.name: Mecha Noodle Bar
places.caption: “Mecha makes a decent pho, in a trendy and aesthetically pleasing bar / restaurant space. The Happy Hour specials look decent as well”

places.name: AMC Broadstreet 7
places.caption: “Certainly on the smaller end for urban AMCs, Broadstreet has a single concession counter, and all of the theatres are all located along a long hallway. That being said, it’s a perfectly lovely place to watch movies.”

places.name: George C. Marshall
places.caption: “Yes, evidently that is George C. Marshall stood at the base of the hill. Awkwardly out of the way, why is he here?”

places.name: Peter Jansen Wessel (Tordenskiold)
places.caption: “Certainly a man that gives off pirate energy”

places.name: Scuba diver statue
places.caption: “This statue sits ready to plunge into the water at any moment. It’s simply perfect for the pier”

places.name: Untuned Bell
places.caption: “Very, very easy to miss at first. You can control the bell with a pedal on the ground.”

places.name: Rådhusplassen
places.caption: “This pier is where you’ll catch some of the boat tours of the fjords. It’s also the back side of the stunning City Hall building, which has a nice view of the water. There’s also a number of statues around the area.”

places.name: Oslo City Hall
places.caption: “Despite City Hall being closed when I visited, the building is just spectacular, and still well worth visiting. Each face is unique, with the best faces being the one from the water, and the one with the clock, in my opinion.”

places.name: Nordraaks plass
places.caption: “Absolutely one of the coolest small parks in the city, if not the whole Nordics. There are giant dragon statues, chained up for our protection.”

places.name: Dronning Sonja
places.caption: “For the Royal Funeral, all of the Royal statues across the country had flowers placed on them, but I don’t think anyone got more than Dronning Sonja. She was absolutely covered.”

places.name: Dronning Maud
places.caption: “Not quite the most prominently featured statue in the Slottenspark, but Maud is located in one of the nicer wooded areas. Maud is depicted in the typical Norwegian style here.”

places.name: Karl Johan Monument
places.caption: “Karl Johan sits high on his horse, towering above on a pedestal, facing the Palace. At the time of the Royal Funeral, the whole area was covered in flowers and flags in respect to the late King. …”

places.name: The Royal Palace
places.caption: “Though the Palace is currently closed, there are still ceremonies held on the Palace grounds, which are open to the public. The Royal Funeral was held here, and the King lied in wake for a period prior.”

places.name: Slottsparken
places.caption: “Slottsparken is the multiblock-sized park that surrounds the royal palace. There’s a pathway which has a series of modern art items along it, and a few more lined by trees. Royal ceremonies are held here, including the recent Royal Funeral (pictured)”

places.name: Aanerud Bakeri Oslo
places.caption: “A small, lovely bakery. Aanerud Bakeri is located down a side street, a bit outside of downtown. The pastries were fantastic, you can skip the drip coffee.”

places.name: Chelsea Market
places.caption: “A block-long food market with a wide variety of permanent vendors, and a mix of other shops. There’s often some cool displays detailing older NYC of years past, and to the history of the building, which was once a biscuit factory.”

places.name: H&H Bagels
places.location: Moynihan Train Hall, 421 8th Ave, New York, NY 10199
places.caption: “The H&H in Penn Station is located between the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall and the Food Court, and while there’s often a line, it does move quickly. This is a fair place to grab a breakfast before heading on your train, or a black and white cookie as a gift.”

places.name: Ashley's Restaurant and Bar
places.caption: “Ashley’s is a neighborhood bar and restaurant with an extensive salad bar and good pasta and burgers. I’ve been here a few times, and everything that I’ve ordered has been pretty consistently solid.”

places.name: Dante West Village
places.caption: “I came to Dante with a party of 20 for a large work event, and they had customized the menu for us, which was pretty unique and a very nice touch. Then the food was absolutely delicious, the chicken was so well cooked, but really everything …”

places.name: Swingers NoMad
places.caption: “A very expansive, indoor miniature golf place, with multiple courses located on the property. It’s a very aesthetically pleasing place, with colorful lights, and good scenes for photography. They also have decent food and drinks. I came here for a work event and we all had a great time”

places.name: Love & Honey Fried Chicken
places.caption: “Really tasty chicken tenders, and a great portion for the cost. They drizzle honey atop, which is just such a great topper”

places.name: Sumalee Thai
places.caption: “I ordered Chicken Pad Thai delivery from here, and it was extremely meh.”

places.name: PrimoHoagies
places.caption: “PrimoHoagies are a great option for a quick and convenient lunch. You can order ahead on their website, and then go pick it up when it’s done, typically in 10mins. I really like their Italian Hoagie.”

places.name: Loco Pez
places.caption: “Loco Pez makes a pretty good burrito, which made for a really sizable lunch”

places.name: Rowhome Coffee - Front Street
places.caption: “Rowhome Coffee makes their Breakfast Sandwiches on Pretzels! How ingenious! The Sausage, Egg, and Cheese ones were delicious and served piping hot. The coffee was fine”

places.name: Gilda
places.caption: “Gilda is a small coffee shop and bakery, but wow do they pack a mighty punch. You can get a drip coffee to stay, and they’ll give you refills, and the pastries are simply out-of-this-world. I’ll have to come back and try the rest of the menu.”

places.name: ReAnimator Coffee
places.caption: “ReAnimator’s a neighborhood coffee spot, but with its central location, it really serves as the hub/heart of the local neighborhood. I like their drip coffee”

places.name: Caletta
places.caption: “Caletta is the bar area of Bastia / Hotel Anna and Bel, and it’s an intimate, lovely spot to stop for a more elevated drink and snack inside of the fancy hotel. …”

places.name: The Viand
places.caption: “While The Viand isn’t an old-school NYC diner, they still get the job done when you’re in need of a breakfast. They’ve got quite large omelettes for a fair price, which come with homemade jam. The coffee was fine”

places.name: Gray's Papaya
places.caption:
“Gray’s Papaya is an institution of the Upper West
Side, most notably for their hot dogs and their papaya juice, but they also sell quite tasty breakfast sandwiches which are only $3 with a cup of coffee. …”

places.name: 7th Street Burger
places.caption: “A good place to stop and get a good, greasy smash burger and some fries. The burgers were better than the fries, and same as with Five Guys, you’ll likely want to get a double if you’re an adult. …”

places.name: El Gallo Taqueria
places.caption: “An option for pretty solid Mexican food for a rather reasonable price  The Carne Asada bowl was decent, and I really like their tacos, with the Carne Asada being a bit better than the Al Pastor”

places.name: Chopt Creative Salad Co.
places.location: Moynihan Train Hall Food Court, 383 W 31st St Ste 037, New York, NY 10001
places.caption: “A great option for a lunch on the go. The salads were reasonably priced and extremely portable. I’d definitely recommend the Greek Salad and adding Chicken, you also get free bread.”

places.name: Moynihan Food Hall
places.caption: “The Moynihan Food Hall (within Penn Station) has a surprisingly wide selection of restaurants to choose from before you catch your train.”

places.name: Schmackary's
places.caption: “Somehow NYC has a bunch of competing gourmet cookie chains. Schmackary’s is a delicious offering, with more reasonably sized cookies, which were all named after Broadway shows. I got the Book of Mormon one, which was great. I’ll be back to try more.”

places.name: Central Park
places.caption: “NYC’s iconic park, and one of the largest urban parks in the world, Central Park is the home to multiple bodies of water, horse stables, and fantastic views of the large residential buildings that line the sides, and skyscrapers at its base.”

places.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
places.caption: “When you’re in Penn Station and need a quick cup of coffee, or a pastry, Blue Bottle isn’t a bad option. They’re situated right in the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall, which is super convenient for those commuting via train.”

places.name: The Ramble
places.caption: “One of the greener and more heavily forested areas of Central Park, which can give this northerly portion a spookier vibe, especially when it’s dark or foggy”

places.name: Dunkin'
places.location: 30th & Market St Station Amtrak Food Court, Philadelphia, PA 19104
places.caption: “This is the Dunkin’ in the main hall, and there’s actually a second, less crowded one, near the SEPTA Regional Rails. America Runs on Dunkin’ especially when it’s the only option in the train hall (but for a Pret down the hall).”

places.name: Manhasset
places.caption: “This LIRR station has a nice indoor portion which provides places to sit down, and to provide some shelter from the elements”

places.name: Philly Halal Gyro
places.caption: “An extremely reasonably priced food truck, serving Halal Food. I liked the Chicken Over Rice, but it was a bit heavy on the hot sauce. I’ll go a bit lighter next time, and may try another meat.”

places.name: The Richmond Shops IGA
places.caption: “A neighborhood grocer with a decent selection of fresh produce, meat, and baked goods. They got all of the national brands, as well as a number of store brands, across products”

places.name: M&M'S New York
places.caption: “The M&M store in Times Square is something of a tourist attraction, as there’s mascots, apparel, and signage recognizing the prominent location, but if you’re not trying to buy some chocolate or a souvenir, there’s little to see or do”

places.name: Grand Bazaar NYC
places.caption: “A weekly market with dozens of vendors arranged in a tennis court, expanding into a high school gymnasium. There were mainly clothing, goods, and art stands, with a food section by the entrance and free Vitamin Water samples.”

places.name: The Met Cloisters
places.location: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
places.caption: “The Met Cloisters is situated atop a hill at the very tippy top of Manhattan, and serves as something of a prize for venturing up to the sleepier portion of the island. …”

places.name: The Strand
places.caption: “Some book stores have this calming ambiance and The Strand has that in heaps. An extremely expansive bookstore with a children’s section in the basement.”

places.name: Brickman's Columbus Ave
places.caption: “An extremely densely packed hardware store that’s likely got what you’re looking for. There were a number of employees ready to help me as well.”

places.name: Crumbl Cookies
places.caption: “The national gourmet, giant cookie and cake chain. Their desserts are good, but certainly more of a treat, or a gift, than a regular item. …”

places.name: 7 Hudson Square
places.caption: “7 Hudson Square is the new home of Disney in New York, both the corporate offices, and the studio spaces living within the building. In the mornings, you can see celebrities entering and exiting the building for their media obligations, and upstairs there’s a theatre for employee only screenings, and a Starbucks”

places.name: The Ravine
places.caption: “There’s a few areas of Central Park where you can get deep enough into the green to forget that you’re still in the heart of the largest city in the country. The Ravine is one of those places, which makes it one of my favorite parts of the megacity”

places.name: Sutton Park
places.caption: “There’s really three attractions in Sutton Park, first the stunning views of the Queensboro Bridge. Then there’s quite a nice statue to a boar in a greener portion of the park. And finally, there’s the views of the Eastern portions of the city.”

places.name: Times Square
places.caption: “Times Square is arguably the most famous place in New York City, and in turn, maybe the most consistently busy. There’s a ton to see, from people watching, to taking in the thousands of neon adverts blaring, there’s much to see in Times Square”

places.name: Inwood Hill Park
places.location: Payson Ave. &, Seaman Ave, New York, NY 10034
places.caption: “If you’re looking for the furthest north point in Manhattan, you’ve found it! Inwood Hill Park sits at the northwest corner of the island, and is equally dense with trees and sparse with humans (on the ground). Though you can nearly always …”

places.name: Bareburger
places.caption: “I really enjoyed Bareburger, they’re a slightly more elevated NYC burger chain, with a bit of a higher price point, which gets you a higher quality burger, with more fun accoutrements. It’s also a sit down restaurant, which caught me by …”

places.name: Non-Violence - Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd
places.location: United Nations Secretariat Building, 405 E 42nd St, New York, NY 10017
places.caption: “I’m certain Non-Violence is a better statue than I’ve reviewed it, but it’s so inaccessible from the street, it’s a true shame. Art shouldn’t be hidden behind walls, and I’d assume the UN (of all organizations) that should understand that”

places.name: 190 St
places.caption: “Quite an interesting metro station. The signage at the upper level is cool and retro, however you have to take an elevator down from there. There’s another entrance, at the ground level, but no stairs or escalators to get you down there”

places.name: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine
places.location: 701 Fort Washington Ave, New York, NY 10040
places.caption: “St. Frances Cabrini Shrine is a church, so if you’re visiting on a Sunday, there will be services going on. There was a front area with a gift shop-appearing section, that was cool even if I didn’t get to see the rest of the building”

places.name: Hustle on George
places.location: Ground Floor/403 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “Really good oat chai lattes, and some great brew coffee. This is one of the only coffee shops open at 5am, and this was just perfect for me.”

places.name: Citi Field
places.caption: “Citi Field is home of the New York Mets, and they also use the stadium for some corporate events and concerts. It’s a great venue with a good variety of vendors. …”

places.name: Hustlers.Syd
places.location: LG, 24 York St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “I came to Hustlers. for a work event, and we ordered drinks and a whole variety of starters and entrees and everything was great. While this place is a bit on the higher end, the quality is certainly on the higher end as well.”

places.name: Qantas International First Lounge Sydney
places.location: Sydney Airport, Terminal 1 Departure Plaza, Mascot NSW 2020, Australia
places.caption: “I stopped by the Qantas First Class Lounge one morning, and was treated like a princess. They made a great breakfast, which came out quickly, and then there were other areas to charge my devices and chill out before my flight”

places.name: Sydney Airport
places.caption: “I quite enjoyed flying out of Sydney Airport. I was in First Class on American Airlines (for work) and the Qantas lounge was very phenomenal, I had such a good breakfast there. The rest of the airport had all of the amenities that you need.”

places.name: Menya City Japanese Noodle Bar
places.caption: “I love Menya City; they’re quick, reasonably priced, and very tasty. The ramen was much better than the katsu.”

places.name: Life From A Suitcase
places.caption: “Love the sentiment of the statue, and the execution is certainly fine as well”

places.name: Windjammers
places.caption: “Ripping statue with a truly nautical view of the downtown skyline.”

places.name: Edward VII
places.caption: “Edward VII is regally and royally presented on his horse. My main complaint with this statue is how hard it is to reach it, and how unfriend it is to pedestrians”

places.name: Chinatown Sydney
places.caption: “Chinatown doesn’t occupy that many blocks, but there is a very high density of business, and two arches to boot.”

places.name: Sydney Souvenirs
places.location: PADDY’s MARKET Cnr Thomas &, Stall 460 Hay St, Haymarket NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “In terms of vibes, Sydney Souvenirs’ was immaculate. No notes. And no comments on the products themselves.”

places.name: Golden Water Mouth
places.caption: “I guess the tree carries some auspiciousness in bark, released by touch; but for the metal fencing, forbidding such an inquiry.”

places.name: Sydney's Water Features - Sydney Culture History Walks
places.caption: “This one must’ve been under construction when I visited because it was all fenced off. I barely knew it was a monument”

places.name: Hay St Market
places.location: Shop R1.05/13 Hay St, Haymarket NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “An indoor market comprised of a maze of restaurants, bakeries, bars, and coffee shops describes just a single portion of Hay St Market. Wander deeper and you’ll find more kitschy, touristy shops with more of a bazaar vibe. The place is way more expansive than one suspects.”

places.name: Dorothea Mackellar Writers Walk Plaque
places.caption: “Quotes from famous Australians and visitors to the island continent are featured all around Circular Quay in circular golden plaques in the pavement”

places.name: Tom Seaver Statue
places.caption: “The statue is situated directly in front of the main facade of the stadium, so it’s easy to frame it in your best shots of the complex”

places.name: Sammy's Woodfired Pizza
places.location: Terminal 4, 1 World Wy, Los Angeles, CA 90045
places.caption: “I came here for breakfast, and ordered the breakfast sandwich with potatoes, and while it was very pricey, it was all delicious and exactly what my body needed.”

places.name: AmericanAirlinesFlagshipLounge
places.caption: “A very nice First Class lounge, don’t get me wrong, but the food was all very fancy, and not at all what I wanted after flying for 15hrs, so I brought in food from downstairs, which they were totally fine with.”

places.name: Qantas International First Lounge Los Angeles
places.caption: “This lounge functions more as a sit down restaurant, where you may need to wait for a table. Not the best snacks outside of the dining area”

places.name: Chelsea Lounge JFK - British Airways & American
places.location: JFK Terminal 8, Central Terminal Area, JFK International Airport, NY 11430
places.caption: “The Chelsea Lounge in JFK is the First Class lounge that services American and British Airways passengers. These lounges are uber luxurious, and have a menu full of delicacies. While they didn’t have the Steak Frites, I didn’t so enjoy the Tartare and Pappardelle before my cross country flight.”

places.name: MOD Pizza
places.caption: “A good place to get a fairly quick and decently cheap, fully customizable pizza. It’s the kind of pie that doesn’t age the best, so eat it quickly”

places.name: Margaret Kuo's Kitchen
places.caption: “Margaret Kuo has long been a quality restaurant chain in the Philly area, and I was happy to find that was still true in the 2020s. Had a great dinner at the Granite Run location, with a variety of Chinese and Pan-Asian dishes. Love that they bring out peanuts and cucumbers as free appetizers.”

places.name: Meghan's
places.caption: “Meghan’s is a staple of Concord Township, as its beloved greasy spoon diner. While they’re often full, it never takes too long for a table to open up. …”

places.name: Martin Place
places.caption: “Sydney’s central business district is littered with giant, majestic, parliament-style buildings, and Martin Place is one of this set. Just stunning on its own, but somehow out of place in its current home”

places.name: K H A O • S O I - カ オ • ソ ー イ
places.location: Level 2/73-75 Liverpool St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “I love Khao Soi, it’s one of my favorite Thai dishes. I’ve been to Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand, where the dish comes from. While the Khao Soi here was fine, it was quite unique in a way that I didn’t love. I’ve never had one so spicy. I often love spice, but with Khao Soi’s pickled taste profile, it just wasn’t my favorite combo.”

places.name: Hyatt Regency Sydney
places.caption: “Set right on Cockle Bay, the Hyatt Regency is a very nice business hotel. I’ve stayed here twice, and both times the rooms were quite large and well stocked. As always, I prefer a usable mini-fridge to one that’s trying to sell me products.”

places.name: AG LEGO® Certified Store Sydney, Pitt St Mall – World’s Largest LEGO® Certified Store
places.location: entry is Via, 400 George Street, Pitt Street Mall, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “This store claims to be the largest LEGO store in the world, and I find that a bit surprising, but sure it’s quite sizable and has a lot of the iconic brick company’s partnerships on display. It’s a fun place to stop while exploring the capital’s downtown.”

places.name: Royal Clock
places.caption: “Queen Victoria Building has two impressive clocks, and the Royal Clock is the bulkier, more castle-resembling one. It’s got its charm, don’t get me wrong, but it’s definitely the lesser of the pair.”

places.name: Great Australian Clock
places.caption: “There are two tiered clocks hanging from Queen Victoria Building and the Great Australian Clock appears to tell the story of the country/continent. The clock has so many details, the longer you inspect it, the more you get from it”

places.name: Queen Victoria Building
places.caption: “The central business district of Syndey has a number of stunning, imperial buildings, and the Queen Victory stands alone as the singular best. From the glass panel on the windows, to the two giant, ornate clocks that hang in either hall, to the historical note in the top floor, this mall has a lot to see apart from the modern day stores.”

places.name: Athena
places.caption: “Small, simple, and elegant, I really enjoyed this statue, and found its existence additive to the city’s beauty”

places.name: The Strand Arcade
places.caption: “Sydney’s downtown should be known for its stunning buildings, and The Strand Arcade, one of many similar arcades, stands near the very top of the class. A tall, straight, singular hall with colorful, slanted, angular panels on the roof, and red carpeting and accenting provide a wonderful visual.”

places.name: Sydney Arcade
places.caption: “There’s a few arcades (in the British sense, meaning a long covered building) in Sydney, but the eponymous one is definitely not the top one. Potentially the LEGO store is the most notable thing about this building, apart from the lovely building itself.”

places.name: Cenotaph
places.caption: “Quite the beautiful monument, one of many in this area, which has an entire pedestrian-only street devoted to it. There were plentiful fresh wreaths when I visited, the area was extremely well kept”

places.name: Royal Australian Regiment Memorial
places.location: Regimental Square, 339A George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “Not a giant monument, in stature, but still an impactful one. You’re just walking around the central business district and suddenly you stumble upon it”

places.name: Rabbit woman, Dogman, vespa and coffee
places.location: Australia Square, 264 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “A lovely statue, a part of a series located in major cities around the work. It does appear that Rabbitwoman was originally holding something (maybe a coffee cup) which is now gone.”

places.name: Sirius Cannon
places.caption: “This is actually a display in two parts: first the more obvious anchor, which is set off the ground, and then the cannon placed outwards, almost to intimidate oneself not to speak ill of the mediocre anchor”

places.name: Sirius Anchor
places.caption: “Quite the large anchor is affixed onto a bit of ground, which itself is presented as a bit of art. Nah”

places.name: Thomas Sutcliff Mort
places.caption: “Ol Tom is situated way up high, leaning on something of a pedestal as he gazes down on the masses”

places.name: Obelisk of Distances
places.caption: “This obelisk almost taunts the reader in saying, “I bet you can’t make it to all of these far off locations”. And one day I hope to return to prove this monument wrong”

places.name: Principal Road Marker
places.caption: “It’s a fine obelisk, and truly one of the finer monuments in Macquarie Place Park, but does an obelisk evoke roads? Maybe it’s a literal representation of a road”

places.name: Macquarie Place Park
places.caption: “A very small park, but it rises above its smaller stature by being jam packed full of monuments, each fairly interesting in its own regard.”

places.name: Bonds of Friendship
places.caption: “I did knot get this piece of art”

places.name: Second World War Servicewomen Memorial
places.location: Jessie Street Gardens, 1-29 Loftus St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
places.caption: “A statue recognizing the unsung and so oft unrecognized heroes of the second world war.”

places.name: Jessie Street Gardens
places.caption: “The tiniest of greeneries, set entirely between giant skyscrapers, and filled with monuments. Jessie Street Gardens is many things, but hardly a garden (in the American sense)”

places.name: Moore Steps
places.caption: “One of the staircases that’ll get you down to the water portion of Circular Quay. Nothing spectacular but it does get the job done.”

places.name: Circular Quay Wharf
places.caption: “The main waterfront area with the Opera House. It’s a great place to get some photos taken. Also, look down, as there’s a series of writers featured in little circles”

places.name: Pennsylvania Railroad World War II Memorial
places.location: William H. Gray III 30th Street Station, 2955 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19104
places.caption: “The signature artwork of 30th St: a humongous statue of an angel holding a fallen man on a pedestal, lined with the names of the fallen.”

places.name: Amtrak Philadelphia Train Station
places.caption: “30th St Station serves both Amtrak and SEPTA, and thus serves as Southeastern PA’s main connector to the region and to the whole Mid-Atlantic area. …”

places.name: AMC 84th Street 6
places.caption: “One of the smaller AMC theatres in the city, and while they don’t have any larger format screens here (no IMAX or Dolby), they do have the fancy recliners; so you get comfort over the visual resolution.”

places.name: The Lake
places.caption: “There’s a few bodies of water within Central Park and The Lake is one of the more prominent ones, although not the largest. But for The Pond, it’s the most downtown body of water, so it gives some of the best reflected skyscraper views. You can also see the Dakota and other iconic UWS buildings from here.”

places.name: Bread and Butter Kitchen
places.caption: “A decent and slightly more reasonably priced lunch option, potentially on account of it being a peninsula away from downtown Annapolis. The omelettes were decent, though nothing was too memorable”

places.name: Tim Hortons
places.location: 6301 Silver Dart Dr Terminal 1, Mississauga, ON L4V 1R9, Canada
places.caption: “This Tim Hortons has a picture of Tim Horton in his hockey get-up. In decade of visiting the Tim Hortons chain, I never knew that it was named after a real guy.”

places.name: The Happy Tummy Bar & Grill
places.caption: “A fine place for dinner, I had a bacon cheeseburger here and it was fine. I’d definitely come back and try the wings and poutine”

places.name: Yellowknife Liquor Store
places.caption: “A very well stocked liquor store, with drinks from all over Canada and the world. I was especially appreciative that they carried nice ice wines from Niagara”

places.name: Raccine Park
places.caption: “In the extremely flat Northwest Territories, Raccine Park contains something of a hill, which has been developed with a memorial”

places.name: Bush Pilots Monument
places.location: 3513 Ingraham Dr #3511, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2E8, Canada
places.caption: “The highest point in Old Town Yellowknife offering sweeping views from the lake to the rest of the city. It’s not too much of a hike to get up there, though it can get fairly icy and slippery”

places.name: Old Town Glassworks
places.location: 3510 McDonald Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2H1, Canada
places.caption: “A lovely glass shop with tons of works made from recycled glasses. I also really appreciate the artwork and craftwork they had in the shop”

places.name: Wing Freak
places.location: Nova Inn, 4401 Franklin Ave 3rd Floor, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1B5, Canada
places.caption: “A decent lunch option, the chicken was well portioned, filling, and tasty. Wing Freak’s strangely located on the 3rd floor of the Nova Inn, but worth the awkward eye contact with the person in the lobby”

places.name: Dock Bridge
places.location: Passaic River, Harrison NJ, Harrison, NJ 07029
places.caption: “The Dock Bridge is the railway bridge which crosses the Passaic River. It’s pretty rusted over, and something of an eyesore, but it’s got its charm”

places.name: Sheetz
places.caption: “Now I’m a Wawa guy, so I’m coming in here with a slant, but the main problem with Sheetz is the speed. When you have a basic order, like a simple breakfast sandwich, you want them ready to go. At Sheetz they actually brag about the fact that they making things to order, which is obscenely slow at most locations, including this one.”

places.name: The Pied Piper of Bedford County
places.caption: “I wasn’t expecting this funny little guy, when I was driving east across Pennsylvania, but life exists to delight, I suppose. What is his story, where is he from, what secrets does he keep?”

places.name: Lookout Point Mt. Ararat
places.caption: “If you stop at the Flight 93 Memorial on the way from Pittsburgh back east, you’ll be driving across Mt. Ararat. You owe it to yourself to stop and take in the vista for a moment.”

places.name: Scenic Overlook
places.caption: “It’s quite the vista, Mt. Ararat. It almost makes me feel like I’m back in the hills of Napa county”

places.name: Post-9/11 U.S. Armed Forces Memorial at Patriot Park
places.caption: “This is an accompanying Memorial, across the street from the official Flight 93 Memorial, this one with flags and the shadow of a person kneeling at a soldier’s memorial. There were only a few flags laid out, far fewer than I was anticipating.”

places.name: Memorial Plaza
places.caption: “The Memorial Plaza is located at the end of a long walkway from the Visitor Shelter, and consists of a large wavy cement wall with the names of the deceased on it. It’s really a touching tribute, where the walk gives you time to reflect.”

places.name: Flight 93 National Memorial - Visitor Center
places.caption: “The Flight 93 Visitor Center itself is perched up on a hill overlooking the disaster’s field, which is now the Memorial Plaza today. The building itself is truly a piece of art, made of simple concrete and glass walls. Unfortunately the architecture functions like something of a wind tunnel so it can get very cold inside.”

places.name: Flight 93 National Memorial
places.caption:
“A touching memorial to the Flight 93 tragedy that occurred on September 11th. There are multiple buildings that encompass the memorial, in some
ways recognizing the field that was scattered here. There’s also a giant wind chime on the way in, in a stunning tower.”

places.name: YINZ Coffee Friendship
places.caption: “Decent coffee, great best, incredible name”

places.name: Shibam Coffee
places.caption: “Very cool aesthetics, and interesting sounding drinks, but I really didn’t enjoy what I got.”

places.name: Pamela's | P&G Diner
places.caption: “Pamela’s is a Pittsburgh institution, and their hotcakes are renowned. They’re like crepes, almost, and you can get them filled with fruit and cream. I always get The Morning After breakfast special, and substitute in Specialty Hot Cakes …”

places.name: Morrow Park
places.caption: “Less a park, and more a statue with some grass, Morrow Park isn’t much to write home about, not to denigrate the perfectly fine statue at its heart.”

places.name: FET-FISK restaurant + bar
places.caption: “Didn’t have a reservation and queued up with a party of 5 about 10 minutes before they opened and got seated at the bar. Fet-Fisk is a very cool upscale restaurant with a variety of excellent seafood and meat options. I had the Tartar, the …”

places.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
places.caption: “Phipps Conservatory is an outstandingly beautiful building, filled with a variety of plants from around the world. However, the most notable thing about this museum isn’t alive, and is entirely Silicon-based. The glass structure of the …”

places.name: Flag Monument
places.caption: “A very simple monument, with a large, gravestone-esque rock and a lone flag on a flagpole. The monument recognizes America on its 150th birthday, and now at year 250, it’s been here for a century.”

places.name: Scotty Dog Statue
places.location: University Center, 5032 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
places.caption: “This statue is new (since I graduated), and I’m not certain how I feel about it. It’s a fine statue, sure, but does it belong in front of the UC? Put it in front of the admissions building”

places.name: Flagstaff Hill
places.caption: “Flagstaff Hill is the far north portion of Schenley Park, which connects Phipps Conservatory with Carnegie Mellon’s campus. It’s a lovely place to sit, and a convenient place to cut across to get to Oakland.”

places.name: Newell-Simon Hall
places.caption: “Newell-Simon Hall is one of the Robots centers on campus, and the building is dressed accordingly. For the last fifteen (plus) years, Tank the Robo-Receptionist has greeted you, and there’s occasionally robotics displays on the first floor. …”

places.name: Steaks West Chester
places.location: 698 E Market St Unit 3, West Chester, PA 19382
places.caption: “These folks make a good cheesesteak, the bread was a bit different from what I was expecting, but not in a bad way”

places.name: Golden Valley Coffee Roasters
places.location: 208 Carter Dr Suite 13B, West Chester, PA 19382
places.caption: “They’ve just got a small little store in their larger production building, but they’ve got their beans a-brewing (just a little bit of drip they offered for free), and a ton of varieties to choose from in-house. I’ll definitely be coming back”

places.name: Ravanesi Pizzeria, Inc.
places.caption: “You need to make a reservation for Ravanesi two weeks in advance, and they ask you how many pizzas you plan to eat that far out. But it’s not hard to see why; they’ve got exceptional pizza dough, which is made into some equally fantastic …”

places.name: Delaware Border State Sign
places.caption: “Difficult to imagine that Delaware has endless anything, much less discoveries.”

places.name: Governor Ritchie Scenic Overlook
places.caption: “This is the first opportunity to stop as you’re leaving Annapolis, and while it may be too early for you to be needing a break, it’s a worthwhile stop as you get two attractions in one.”

places.name: Gold Star Family Monument
places.caption: “While certainly the secondary monument on the hill, the Gold Star Families Memorial is almost the more visually impressive of the two. I love the shadow play of the sculpture.”

places.name: Maryland World War II Memorial
places.caption: “This Memorial is an impressive visual, on a prominent hillside as you leave Annapolis to go north. The WWII Memorial is a somber site, comprised of an amphitheater of sorts, built up to a star and flags.”

places.name: Liberty Bell Replica
places.caption: “Situated right at the entrance of St. John’s College, this Liberty Bell is a replica of the original bell before it was cracked, purportedly”

places.name: Guardians of the First Amendment Memorial
places.caption: “Visiting this one in April 2026 felt especially prescient as we appear to be living through history. It’s funny how things repeat themselves, almost”

places.name: Kunta Kinte - Alex Haley Memorial
places.caption: “While the statues themselves aren’t the most impressive, I did appreciate the creative arrangement, and the powerful placards scattered around the piers. The memorial is very centrally located in downtown Annapolis, stop for a moment and appreciate it”

places.name: Mills Fine Wine and Spirits
places.caption: “Quite an expansive wine and spirits store with varietals from all over the world. I like the little maps of all the wine growing regions of each country’s section, and really appreciate that they carry wine and mead.”

places.name: Reclaimed of Annapolis
places.caption: “An upper-end thrift shop for furniture, much of which has been fixed up since its inception”

places.name: Annapolis Essentials
places.caption: “If you’re looking to pick up some Old Bay sweatpants on your trip to Maryland, Annapolis Essentials is the place for you. It’s all very touristy, you won’t find anything small and local here.”

places.name: Welcome to Maryland sign
places.caption: “It would be annoying to be the person that they left behind, but at least they made the rule afterwards”

places.name: Buffalo Wild Wings
places.caption: “Large beers and decent wings with a large amount of TVs on every wall playing a variety of sports, what more could you ask for”

places.name: South Station
places.caption: “South Station is one of the major train stations in Boston, of which there are a few. The building itself is fairly unique looking though honestly I don’t love it. I wish they had more food options inside”

places.name: Kendall/MIT
places.caption: “One of the quirkier T stops that I’ve visited, with a few attractions in the station itself. The Red line stops here”

places.name: Point Park
places.caption: “The self-proclaimed Most Innovative Square Mile on the Planet, and why not. Who is honestly going to try to prove otherwise”

places.name: The Mall
places.caption: “There are two interconnected green lawns on Carnegie Mellon’s main campus: The Cut, extending to Forbes, and The Mall, with its iconic shot extended out to Pitt’s Cathedral of Learning.”

places.name: The Fence
places.caption: “The most iconic landmark on Carnegie Mellon’s campus. The Fence has strict rules, it can only be painted by hand and by brush (no rollers), and it can only be painted after midnight. To hold The Fence, you need to keep two (or more) people …”

places.name: The Bride of Penn Ave
places.caption: “A hauntingly beautiful painting of the Penn Ave of Pittsburgh yester. Maybe we’ll get back there one day”

places.name: Pittsburgh Glass Center
places.caption: “Pittsburgh Glass Center is a combination studio space and teaching studio, where you can take classes to learn the craft of glassblowing. The studio had an exhibit filled with the students’ art, and it was simply exceptional; with some …”

places.name: Friendship Perk & Brew
places.caption: “Friendship Perk & Brew is local coffee shop and sit-down breakfast restaurant has a very homey feel, with some ok java and good pastries.”

places.name: täkō
places.caption:
“A hip and modern taqueria offering a diversity of elevated tacos in a smaller dark multilevel bar
room. The eponymous Tako taco is their speciality, and while it’s very good, it’s not my favorite.”

places.name: Gates Center for Computer Science
places.location: Gates Center for Computer Science, 5000 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
places.caption: “Built when the Foundation was still called the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the building’s most notable feature is the Guggenheim-esque spiral staircase that oh so slowly snakes down the mainly vertical building.”

places.name: The Cut
places.caption: “The Cut is the nickname for the central lawn that goes from Forbes Avenue to Hunt Library, including the Fence. I’ve always believed that it’s named that because you need to “cut” across it to get to the other half of the buildings”

places.name: Walking to the Sky
places.caption: “Walking to the Sky is one of the more prominent artworks on Carnegie Mellon’s campus, maybe second only to The Fence. That being said, I, among many other alums (and I’m sure current day students), really don’t love it.”

places.name: Bakery Square
places.caption: “Bakery Square is a shopping and building complex with a few parking garages, gyms, restaurants and corporate offices. Many of the photos included are from Google Pittsburgh, which is located across two of the buildings here, and includes an employee (and their guest) exclusive cafe.”

places.name: Back Creek Books
places.caption: “This store has quite the collection of rare and eclectic books. Though the store isn’t especially expansive, there were half a dozen cabinets each with a dozen unique books.”

places.name: Colonial Annapolis Historic District
places.caption: “Colonial Annapolis is a historic cobblestone area, with a number of notable events in its distant history. Today it’s a lovely shopping area, albeit a bit touristy, with tons of Navy men and women around.”

places.name: State House Cannon
places.caption: “The cannon looks a bit rough, but it’s had quite the storied history, immortalized with a plaque on it. The thing is mounted on the State House hill, point outwards.”

places.name: The Annapolis Pottery
places.caption: “An Annapolis institution that I’ve been visiting for my whole life. Rooms upon rooms of every kind of pottery for every use that you can think of, and a few more. If you’re visiting Annapolis for a day trip, perusing this pottery is a must.”

places.name: Baron Johann de Kalb
places.caption: “Located on the westside of the State House, de Kalb is standing shaking his fist to the sky. He really embodies the great energy of the capitol grounds.”

places.name: Maryland State House
places.caption: “Annapolis is a town built around a hill by the water, with the State House perched atop the mound. That means that you can see this magnificent building from nearly the whole of Annapolis. In the spring the cherry blossoms really add to the aesthetic. There’s a few statues and a cannon on the grounds”

places.name: William Preston Lane Jr. Memorial Bay Bridge
places.caption: “The Chesapeake Bay Bridge truly is an impressive bridge to traverse because of its length and various segments with their distinct regions. If you’re afraid of heights, looking around may give you a trippy sensation”

places.name: Passing Through mural
places.caption: “An extremely difficult mural to capture from Amtrak, as you need to be sitting on the right side on a southbound train to/through Philadelphia”

places.name: Galaxy Park
places.caption: “A cute little triangular cement park with a globe of sorts in the middle of a fountain. The nicest thing about this very non-green park is the surrounds”

places.name: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Boston
places.caption: “Stayed here for a work event, and the hotel itself was extremely beautiful, I heard it used to be a jail. My room was in the main building, which seemed to be unique among my coworkers, regardless I really enjoyed my room and my stay.”

places.name: Viale
places.caption: “A lovely place for dinner that can accommodate large parties. I really enjoyed the oysters, the octopus, and the steak when I came here for a work event.”

places.name: Broad Nosh Bagels
places.caption: “One of the better bagel options in the UWS, though don’t get the salt bagel. It was entirely covered in rock salt and way overly done. …”

places.name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir
places.caption: “The Reservoir is the largest body of water in Central Park and one of its most notable landmarks. You can’t go out onto the water, and you certainly can’t swim in it. There is a running track that goes along the perimeter of the body of water, which enforces a single direction of traffic, counter-clockwise.”

places.name: Peace Fountain by Greg Wyatt
places.caption: “The Peace Fountain may be my singular favorite statue in the whole of New York City. There’s so much going on, it’s chaotic, it’s messy, it’s fantastic. It’s surrounded by a ring of smaller animal statues, complimenting the animal parts that encompass the larger artwork.”

places.name: Tom's Restaurant
places.caption: “Let’s be real, you’re not coming to Tom’s for the food, you’re coming here because of the show. And while Tom’s certainly caters to the fans by having a number of pictures of the cast, it’s functionally just a typical NYC diner. The Lumberjack was pretty decent”

places.name: Kossar's Bagels & Bialys
places.caption: “Kossar’s makes an excellent breakfast sandwich, I went with my typical Sausage, Egg, and Cheese on an Everything Bagel, and I loved what I got. They brew La Colombe coffee, and my only complaint is that their cups are horrible; it still leaked through two cups”

places.name: Hall of Saurischian Dinosaurs
places.caption: “One of my favorite parts of the History Museum, filled with Dinosaurs stretching across vast halls, and towering over crowds. But be wary, this is also one of the busiest parts of the building, with a heavy density of people filling every nook and cranny.”

places.name: Horace Greeley Monument
places.location: 894-900 Ave Of The Amer, New York, NY 10001
places.caption: “Horace has the misfortune of having both an old looking face and an old sounding name. At least they gave the old guy a chair to spend eternity in. They’ve also surrendered him with flowers, making the whole thing look almost like a tomb. RIP Ol’ Horace”

places.name: Carl Schurz Park
places.location: East 86th Street &, East End Ave, New York, NY 10028
places.caption: “Carl Schurz Park is located on the East River in the Upper East Side, and contains a section of John Finley walk and Gracie Mansion. There’s also a Peter Pan Statue and a lot of green shrubbery, it’s a fine place to go for a break or a bit of a walk.”

places.name: Penn Station
places.caption: “NY Penn Station has a worse reputation than it deserves. As someone that regularly uses Amtrak, I really like the aesthetic design of the station, the availability of the subways underneath, and the selection of restaurants and shops and their hours.”

places.name: Eleanor Roosevelt Memorial
places.caption: “Eleanor Roosevelt was the first female aviatrix to fly across the Pacific Ocean, until everything changed when she vanished one day from her house never to be seen again. People have searched everywhere for her plane, but no one knows where it went”

places.name: Läderach
places.caption: “A gourmet chocolatier with a higher price point which makes decent gifts for loved ones. The store has a human-sized statue of liberty made out of chocolate inside, and heaps of sheets of chocolate. They also tend to give out free samples as well.”

places.name: Morningside Park
places.caption: “While not as famous as Central Park or Riverside Park, Morningside Park is one of Manhattans great parks. Located above Central Park on the westside, this park offers a number of steep, hilly paths, and a serene lake with a purported waterfall.”

places.name: Gracie Mansion Conservancy
places.location: 181 East End Ave, New York, NY 10128
places.caption: “Honestly, I didn’t realize that Gracie Mansion was located here when I was intending to see Peter Pan, but this was something of a nice surprise. You really can’t get up close to the building at all, which makes sense, for security purposes.”

places.name: Mount Tom
places.caption: “Less of a mountain and more of a big honking rock, you can climb Mount Tom and get a decent overview of the Warsaw Monument, but on account of the heavy tree cover, not much else. Still, it’s a fun place to do a bit of rock scrambling.”

places.name: AMC DINE-IN Painters Crossing 9
places.caption: “One of the dine-in AMC Theatres, which will still sell you popcorn, pretzels, and the classic movie snacks and drinks, but they also have a fuller food and drink menu which they’ll deliver to your seat. …”

places.name: Yellowknife Visitor Centre
places.location: Centre Square Mall, 5014 50 St, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3R6, Canada
places.caption: “This isn’t the nicest spot in downtown Yellowknife, but there’s information and free maps here. They’ll also give you a little pin and a certificate for crossing the 60th parallel”

places.name: ReLeaf NT
places.caption: “A decent shop. Broad supply and reasonable prices, all that you need. They also gave me popcorn which was pretty sweet”

places.name: Yellowknife Public Library
places.location: 2nd Floor, Centre Square Mall, 5022 49 St, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3R8, Canada
places.caption: “The Library’s on the second floor of the mall, and features a small art collection with pieces around the floor. It’s a nice place to stop and support as a visitor”

places.name: Northern Souvenirs & Gifts
places.caption: “A fair place to buy Canadian, Yellowknife, and Northwest Territory apparel and keepsakes. The store is very densely packed with goods”

places.name: Chan Lake Territorial Park
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0M0, Canada
places.caption: “An moderate vista, which proves to be a fine place to stop, when you need some respite. I’ll add, this had some of the deepest snowbanks that I found”

places.name: Zhati Kue Friendship Centre
places.caption: “A community center with some very friendly people inside”

places.name: Community Arbour
places.caption: “When I showed up at the Arbour there wasn’t a soul to be found, however, there was a decently well kept fire, with fresh wood next to the hearth. I appreciate whoever left this warm treat, but wish they’d stuck around”

places.name: Our Lady of Providence
places.location: DehCho Dr, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0A7, Canada
places.caption: “An aesthetically crisp white church sat right on the water. It’s only open during the warmer months, so I can only assume the insulation isn’t the best”

places.name: Kakisa River Territorial Park
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
places.caption: “A stunning valley, covered in a sheet of sparkling white, with a simple - and seldom tread - bridge spanning it”

places.name: Lady Evelyn Falls Territorial Park
places.caption: “Completely inaccessible and covered in snow”

places.name: McNallie Creek Territorial Park Day Use Area
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
places.caption: “Really spectacular looking falls when covered in snow. Nothing quite like those icicles dangling over the cliff”

places.name: Woodland Wok & Grill
places.location: 66 Woodland Dr #8, Hay River, NT X0E 0R2, Canada
places.caption: “For lunch, it seemed like the buffet was the only option, which I was ok with. They food was fine, very much mall Chinese food, similar to what I grew up eating in The States”

places.name: NWT Centennial Library
places.location: 75 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
places.caption: “This is one of the nicest places to stop in Hay River, the NWT Centennial Library really is a nexus for local information. They also had some interesting local papers that they let me keep as a souvenir”

places.name: Katlodeeche First Nation
places.location: Hay River 1, Hay River, NT X0E, Canada
places.caption: “Much easier to access in the months when the river is frozen. Just across the water from Hay River”

places.name: The Forks
places.caption: “For half of the year, this portion of Hay River is frozen over, and it becomes an ice road connecting the two parts of the city across the water”

places.name: Marine Transportation Services - Shipyard
places.location: 1 104 Ave, Hay River, NT X0E 0R2, Canada
places.caption: “In the winter, the ships freeze into the harbor, and really have a nice visual from the beach”

places.name: Pumphouse Beach
places.caption: “A peculiar place to visit in the colder months, as all that you can see (over the parking lot’s snowbank), is endless, nearly perfectly untouched snow. Cool vista, kinda windy, you can skip this one”

places.name: Parks Canada Fire Management Regional Fire Base
places.caption: “Not a bad place to watch the northern lights (sadly, not seen, and thus not pictured); it’s nearly totally dark out here”

places.name: Town of Fort Smith
places.location: 174 McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “I spent a day in Fort Smith and had a really good time there! It’s a lovely little town nestled up at the eastern NWT/Alberta border. Visit Anna’s Restaurant, and get a coffee at Javapunks while you’re there”

places.name: Kaeser's Stores Ltd
places.location: 76-80 Breynat St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “A very well-stocked supermarket for the remoteness of the city. I really appreciated that they carried Sap drinks”

places.name: Fort Smith Fire Dept
places.location: 70 Breynat St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “The temperature clocks in front of the Fire Dept display the power of the (sub-)Arctic sun. In March, as the sun is staying up for longer, the clock faces will span 20°C depending on how long they’ve been baking in the sun.”

places.name: Fort Smith Visitor Centre
places.location: 149 McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “The Visitor Centre was closed when I visited in March, and they appeared to be doing some reservations. I hope it’s nice when it reopens”

places.name: Wood Buffalo Inn
places.caption: “Only stayed here for a single night, but the accommodations were great. The Inn is structured as a motel, but the rooms are stocked like entire apartments. If I come back to Fort Smith, I’ll definitely stay here again.”

places.name: Javapunks (Cafe)
places.location: 101 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “Every town in the Northwest Territories has their cool coffee shop, and Javapunks is Fort Smith’s. They’ve got a decent drink coffee in a hip and cozy location. If I come back, I’d love to stay and do some work from here.”

places.name: NSIXTY Trading Company Ltd.
places.location: 101 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “N60 Trading Company is a really interesting, well stocked hobby store. It’s such a gem for this kind of store to exist in such a remote location. I’m glad the people of the far north can get supplies for their hobbies, and games for the long and dark winters.”

places.name: Northern Life Museum & Cultural Centre and Gift Shop
places.location: 110 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “I’m sad that I didn’t get to go into the Northern Life Museum, despite them claiming to be open. I even called them to no avail, a real shame”

places.name: Anna's Restaurant
places.location: 338 Calder Ave, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
places.caption: “Anna’s Restaurant was the only place that I ate while I was in Fort Smith, because after stopping in for brunch, I simply had to return for dinner to try the pizza (I got a calzone). Everything I had here was simply delicious, especially the incredible bread, and the towns were an absolute delight to talk to.”

places.name: Mountain Portage
places.location: Unnamed Road, Wood Buffalo, AB T0P, Canada
places.caption: “A bit harrowing to reach in winter, you’ll need to walk from the Portage Parking, marked on the map, with skis or snowmobiles also being options. The views truly aren’t the best, but hey, it’s something to see”

places.name: Mountain Portage Parking
places.caption: “At least in winter, this is really as far as you’re going to want to drive. As a bonus for stopping here, you can get a bit of a view of the frozen water below. …”

places.name: Little Buffalo River Falls Territorial Park
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0P0, Canada
places.caption: “There are so few places between Hay River and Fort Smith, and even fewer which are open in the winter. Little Buffalo River Falls were open and generally accessible, though not the most impressive. Still worth stopping (but keep that engine running).”

places.name: Wood Buffalo National Park of Canada
places.caption: “A wonderful place to go for a drive. But know, it’s very very sparse, with quite few people traversing the roads. During winter, play it safe and don’t stray too far off the main roads”

places.name: Big Buffalo River
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R7, Canada
places.caption: “Big must be relative, and not to the region”

places.name: Pine Point Bridge
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R7, Canada
places.caption: “In a land of sparseness, everything is notable, and this bridge was lovely, vibrant hue of green, and gave some interesting views during wintertime”

places.name: Esso
places.location: 921 MacKenzie Hwy Ss 22, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
places.caption: “A full service gas station with some decently reasonable prices. Because it’s located on the main road, it’s easy to stop here just before leaving town”

places.name: Georginas Place Thrift Shop
places.location: 69 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
places.caption: “A small, well stocked thrift shop located in what feels like a house”

places.name: Hay River Tourist Information
places.location: McBryan Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
places.caption: “While the center was shut when I came by in late March, they did have some of the finest art in the region on display just outside, and that was plenty for me”

places.name: Rat Lake
places.location: Rat Lake, MacKenzie County, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
places.caption: “Completely inaccessible from Indian Cabins, sadly”

places.name: Indian Cabins Trading Post
places.location: Hwy 35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
places.caption: “As you head south from the 60th Parallel by Hay River, Indian Cabins Trading Post is the first thing that you’ll hit south of the border. And what a wonderful place to stop, if only for Screw Stewie, a dog that’s all too excited to meet you”

places.name: Welcome to the Northwest Territories Sign
places.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
places.caption: “In terms of border signs, this one is quite impressive, especially when compared to its contemporaries - the Welcome to Alberta sign opposite it and the signs by Fort Smith. The whole place is a ghost town if you make the journey in winter, with the exception of the odd car flying by”

places.name: Welcome to Mackenzie County Sign
places.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
places.caption: “Much better than the Alberta sign a hundred meters in front of it. You got a sun and everything on the sign, it’s doing its own thing”

places.name: Welcome to Alberta Sign
places.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
places.caption: “Albertans, let’s be honest. This sign isn’t bringing your province the glory that it deserves. You gotta dream bigger, especially when the NWT sign opposite yours is so much bigger and nicer”

places.name: Sixtieth Parallel Territorial Park
places.location: Mackenzie Hwy, Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
places.caption: “If you’re looking to see the inside of any of the buildings, I’d recommend visiting in the summer months”

places.name: Sixtieth Parallel Territorial Park Visitor Centre
places.location: Hwy 1, South Slave Region, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
places.caption: “Rating this on aesthetics alone, as the whole place was shut for winter when I visited in late March. With pristine, untouched snow, and tall ordinary trees surrounding the simple structure, the aesthetic was fine”

places.name: Alexandra Falls Observation Deck
places.location: 1 Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 1G3, Canada
places.caption: “This deck is situated out on the cliff face, above the falls, giving a sweeping view of Alexandra Falls and the lower river basin”

places.name: Alexandra Falls
places.location: 1 Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 1G3, Canada
places.caption: “Completely frozen in the winter, the Alexandra Falls make for a memorable visit regardless of the time of the year”

places.name: Alexandra Falls Territorial Park Day Use Area
places.location: Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
places.caption: “One of the few stops along the NWT Highways which was actually open and accessible during the winter. The trail was mostly packed snow leading to the observation pavilion.”

places.name: Big Lake
places.location: 2-4 Courtoreille St, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
places.caption: “Big Lake is the only real coffee shop in Hay River, and they make a decent cup of coffee and muffin. They also have more full meals, and for more meals than breakfast, but I never tried either; maybe my loss.”

places.name: Welcome to Enterprise Sign
places.caption: “Simple sign, could be a bit more fantabulous”

places.name: Riverview Cineplex
places.location: 25 Studney Dr, Enterprise, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
places.caption: “With Yellowknife’s movie theatre now being shut, this may be the last cinema in the NWT. Sadly I couldn’t support them, I hope they survive and keep fighting the good fight”

places.name: Junction of Highways 1 and 2
places.caption: “You’d think that there’d be more here, but in winter, this area was exceptionally dead except for the trucks passing by. Whether you’re going to/from Fort Smith, Hay River, or Yellowknife, you’ll be passing through Enterprise which is entirely comprised by this intersection.”

places.name: Information Board
places.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
places.caption: “This information board is located at the intersection of Route 1 and Route 3, as 3 dead-ends into 1. It’s a fine board, I guess it’s something to note”

places.name: Deh Cho Bridge
places.location: South Slave Region, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
places.caption: “The Northwest Territories is so sparse of human creations that any are notable. Arguably, the Deh Cho Bridge is the most spectacular landmark outside of the few cities of the NWT, with a stark prominence visible from miles away on either …”

places.name: Big River Service Centre LP
places.location: 1 NT-3 Lot 3, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
places.caption: “One of the better places to stop on the route connecting Hay River and Yellowknife, with reasonably priced gas and some hot food, snacks, and drinks. If you’ve got the time, stop off in Fort Providence”
